archetype.name: Pocket Passer (vertical)
archetype.definition: A rhythm thrower who almost never leaves the pocket and earns his value pushing the ball past the sticks, especially between the numbers, rather than through scrambles or the quick game.

report.headline: Volume is real, the vertical game is real; the protection is the problem.
report.take:
Jordan Love is producing a different season than last year's, not a better one. He leads the league with 2838 passing yards and ranks 2nd at 283.8 a game, nearly 60 more per game than in 2025. His efficiency has gone the other way: 0.142 EPA per dropback ranks 15th, after he finished 5th by EPA per play last year. The volume is mostly structural. Green Bay's run game ranks last in the league in EPA, Josh Jacobs has played only three games, and the offense passes more than situation predicts (7th in pass rate over expected). Love is carrying a team that can't run, and that means more dropbacks in worse spots.

The passing profile is clear. Everything good happens 10+ yards downfield: 0.538 EPA per attempt on those throws, with intermediate (0.531) and deep (0.545) nearly identical, and the middle of the field (0.422) as his best area. Underneath, the offense gives back almost all of it. Throws behind the line run at -0.177 EPA and everything under 10 air yards at 0.02, so screens and dump-offs are acting as a substitute for a run game that doesn't exist, and they don't work as one. Christian Watson is the main beneficiary at 0.497 EPA per target. Matthew Golden draws more volume (102 targets) at a far more ordinary 0.225.

The early-season accuracy dip has corrected. His CPOE is down 3.4 points from 2025 and his bad-throw rate is up, but that is a September story. He posted CPOE of -9.7, -13.6 and -8.5 in the first three weeks, then +11.7 and +25.6 against Carolina and New England, and his last three games show a 12.3 CPOE and 0.252 EPA per dropback. The cost of that stretch is sacks: a 10.2% sack rate over the last three, capped by eight sacks against Minnesota's No. 1 defense. He is getting the ball out faster than ever (2.58 seconds, down from 2.89). The sacks are coming anyway, which points at the line more than at him: the starting right guard is out, and so is his veteran fill-in.

Late in close games he has been poor (-0.283 EPA, no TDs, two picks on 36 plays), and red-zone EPA is negative despite 13 touchdowns there. Neither sample is large enough to call a trait. Read together, though, they say this offense struggles when the field shrinks and the defense knows a pass is coming. That describes a team without a run game more than it describes a quarterback who shrinks in big moments.

strengths.title: Middle-of-field intermediate and deep throws
strengths.body: Throws of 10+ air yards produce 0.538 EPA per attempt and most of his passing value, and the middle of the field is his most efficient direction. This is how he has always played: his aDOT and aggressiveness have sat in the same narrow band every season since 2023. It lasts as long as his receivers can win vertically.

strengths.title: Accuracy has snapped back
strengths.body: After a September of negative CPOE, his last three games show a 12.3 CPOE and 0.252 EPA per dropback. That stretch is much closer to his 2025 form (5.5 CPOE, 8th) than the opening weeks were. The early slump looks like a blip, not decline, though some of the recent spike came against soft defenses.

strengths.title: Lethal from under center
strengths.body: On 70 under-center plays he posts 0.36 EPA with a 15.7 CPOE. From shotgun those numbers drop to 0.073 and -1.9. The under-center looks, where defenses must respect a run, are his cleanest throws, and the split argues LaFleur should use them more even with a run game this bad.

concerns.title: Protection is breaking down
concerns.body: His sack rate over the last three games is 10.2%, well above his season mark, and Minnesota sacked him eight times in Week 10. His time to throw is the fastest of his career, so this isn't him holding the ball. It lines up with the right guard (87% of snaps) and his replacement both being out, behind an offense that ranks 23rd in hit rate allowed. Until the interior is healthy, expect sacks to keep stealing drives.

concerns.title: No run game, no easy yards
concerns.body: Green Bay ranks 32nd in rushing EPA, and the short passes meant to replace the run (throws behind the line at -0.177 EPA, everything under 10 air yards at 0.02) don't. That inflates his volume but caps his efficiency: he has to win downfield to stay ahead of the chains. It is unlikely to change until Jacobs returns.

concerns.title: Close-and-late and red-zone dips
concerns.body: In one-score fourth quarters he is at -0.283 EPA with no TDs and two INTs. His red-zone EPA is negative despite 13 TDs there. Both are small samples. Both also fit a team that can't run when the field shrinks, so this reads more as context than as a flaw in him.

trend.note: The path is upward with dips that line up with the opponent. After negative EPA in two of the first three weeks, he was positive every week from Week 3 through Week 9, peaking at 18.5 against New England. Then Minnesota's No. 1 defense sacked him eight times. Both of his ugliest games came against that defense.

nextGame.headline: Rams take away the deep shots but rarely hit the quarterback
nextGame.body:
The Rams are a bad matchup on paper: 3rd in defensive EPA, 4th against the pass, 1st against the run, and 3rd in EPA allowed on deep throws. That last ranking is aimed right at the part of his game that produces most of his value. They allow only 219.3 passing yards a game to quarterbacks (4th fewest). There is one real opening. Los Angeles ranks 28th in hit rate and 19th in sack rate, so after an eight-sack game this is the first front in a while that shouldn't swarm him. Against the league's top run defense, Green Bay will throw a lot. With his line patched together, the question is whether volume and a clean pocket outweigh a secondary that limits big plays.

Availability on his side: right guard Sean Rhyan is out with an expected return date of this game (an estimate), and Kevin Zeitler, who was set to replace him, is also out. Josh Jacobs (finger surgery) is out too, which keeps the run game where it is. Skyy Moore's ankle is reportedly not serious, and he is a minor piece. On the Rams' side, center Coleman Shelton is doubtful and guard Steve Avila is out. Their interior line is depleted, which helps Green Bay's 10th-ranked pass rush shorten Rams drives. Davante Adams is reportedly targeting this game for his return from IR. He would sharpen a Rams offense that already ranks 8th in EPA and could push the scoring pace.

keyMatchups.title: Deep game vs. a top deep defense
keyMatchups.body: His 10+ air-yard throws drive the offense, and the Rams allow -0.252 EPA on deep passes, 3rd best. If Watson can't win over the top, Love has to live on the short game, which has produced almost nothing this year. Patience and middle-of-field intermediate throws are the path.

keyMatchups.title: Patched line vs. a quiet rush
keyMatchups.body: The Rams' 28th-ranked hit rate is the friendliest pass-rush profile he has seen lately. It should give his reshuffled interior line some breathing room after the eight-sack loss.

keyMatchups.title: Run game shut off entirely
keyMatchups.body: The league's worst rushing offense meets the league's best run defense. Expect a pass-heavy script: good for his volume, bad for his efficiency on predictable downs. The Rams also hold lead backs to -0.2 EPA per play, so dump-offs won't bail him out.

nextGame.watch: Whether the Rams' soft pass rush gives him enough time to find intermediate throws in the middle of the field. If his sack total stays low, he can grind out a solid day even without deep completions.

restOfSeason.body:
The volume is sustainable because its cause is: a bottom-ranked run game and a team that leans pass. A pace of 4825 yards and 34 TDs is a fair baseline if he stays healthy. His accuracy rebound since September looks real given his 2025 track record, so efficiency should settle above his season mark but below the last-three spike, which was padded by Carolina and New England.

The swing is protection. With both guards out, the 10.2% sack rate of the last three games is the biggest threat to his EPA and to drives finishing. A Jacobs return would also help, making the under-center looks he thrives on more credible and taking some predictability off the pass. Expect two more meetings' worth of volatility against elite defenses and big lines against soft ones.
swingFactors: Health of the interior line (Rhyan, Zeitler)
Josh Jacobs' return to a last-ranked run game
Watson staying healthy as the vertical target

confidence.note: Ten games with a clear career baseline, but line injuries and opponent quality swing his games hard.
